**Top four interstate wars (1800 – 2011) by combatant deaths (Our World in Data)**  

| Rank | War | Combatant deaths |
|------|-----|-------------------|
| 1 | **World War II** | 21.1 million |
| 2 | **World War I** | 7.11 million |
| 3 | **Second Sino‑Japanese War** | 1.69 million |
| 4 | **Chinese Civil War** | 1.2 million |

These figures are taken from Our World in Data’s interactive chart “Wars ranked by death toll, 1800‑2011,” which lists combat‑fighting deaths in conventional wars for the period 1800‑2011 [#1](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/deaths-in-wars-by-war-1800-2011-bar-chart).

> *The chart’s top‑selection box shows the four wars with the highest combatant deaths in descending order: World War II, World War I, Second Sino‑Japanese War, and the Chinese Civil War.*

These four conflicts constitute the most lethal interstate wars in terms of combatant casualties during the specified period.

These figures are taken from Our World in Data’s interactive chart “Wars ranked by death toll, 1800‑2011,” which lists combat‑fighting deaths in conventional wars for the period 1800‑2011 [#1](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/deaths-in-wars-by-war-1800-2011-bar-chart).

> *The chart’s top‑selection box shows the four wars with the highest combatant deaths in descending order: World War II, World War I, Second Sino‑Japanese War, and the Chinese Civil War.*

These four conflicts constitute the most lethal interstate wars in terms of combatant casualties during the specified period.
